basis.text: Wadsworth, commanding the division on the field, wrote on 4 Jul 1863 that 'at this time (about 10.15 a. m.) our gallant leader fell' (Official Records 27/1, p. 266); Doubleday's report of 14 Dec 1863 gives about 10.15 for the same event (p. 245). Howard's 11.15 (dispatch of 5 p.m., p. 696) is a reckoning from news that reached him about 11.30 (p. 702). Weld, Reynolds' aide, rode to Meade about 10:00, so Reynolds was alive then. No source gives 10:30 or 10:40-10:50.

default.label: About 10:15: Wadsworth's report of 4 Jul 1863 and Doubleday's report; Howard's 11.15 is a later reckoning
default.note: Both 10.15 readings come from officers of the First Corps and are hedged ('about'); the default carries about a quarter of an hour either way. One officer's account (Hall's battery, ordered in by Reynolds, 'opened ... at 10.45') would put the fall after 10.45 if its clock is exact; that tension is why the class is weighted and why 11:15 stays selectable.

weighing.summary: Howard's note of 5 p.m. is a better class of writing (a dispatch of the day) than Wadsworth's report of three days later, but its writer was elsewhere and relays news, so on this point the vantage of the man on the field outweighs the class. Two reports of the First Corps, Wadsworth's of 4 Jul 1863 and Doubleday's of 14 Dec 1863, put the fall of Reynolds at about 10.15 a.m. Howard's note of 5 p.m. says 11.15, but Howard was in the town, learned of the death about 11.30 (his report; Schurz agrees on the hour of the news and says Reynolds had 'just' been killed), so 11.15 is a reckoning from news, not an observation. Weld's diary shows Reynolds alive about 10:00: sent with a message, he reached Meade at 11.20 after an hour and twenty minutes. No source gives 10:30 or 10:40 to 10:50; the first values of the plan are unsourced. One tension is not removed: Hall's report (Wainwright prints it) says Reynolds ordered his battery into position and that it opened at 10.45, which, if exact, puts Reynolds alive after 10:45; Hall's hour is the opening of his own fire, not an hour for the death, and it is carried as a reason the default is weighted, not settled.
weighing.who: Wadsworth commanded the division whose brigades Reynolds was placing; Doubleday took the corps when Reynolds fell; Weld was Reynolds' aide; Howard commanded the Eleventh Corps, which was still on the road; Schurz arrived with the news. Hall commanded the Maine battery Reynolds placed.
weighing.when: Howard's note: afternoon of 1 Jul 1863 (dispatch). Wadsworth: 4 Jul 1863 (three days). Weld: diary of July 1863, published 1912. Howard's report: 31 Aug 1863. Schurz: 20 Aug 1863. Doubleday: 14 Dec 1863. By rank Howard's dispatch (rank 6) outranks Wadsworth's report (rank 5), but its writer was elsewhere and relays; the writer on the field who says the hour wins on vantage, and the dispatch is contradicted by Weld's ride only for the lower bound.
weighing.where: Wadsworth was on McPherson Ridge with the leading brigades; Doubleday arrived behind the left wing and 'learned' of the death a little later; Weld left Reynolds about 10:00 and met the news on his way back; Howard was in the town (on a building) and was told about 11.30; Schurz joined him near the cemetery.
weighing.how_knew: Wadsworth gives the hour in a parenthesis and does not say whether he saw the fall; Doubleday learned it; Howard was told; Weld saw Reynolds alive. None quotes a watch for the fall.
weighing.clock: All the Union writers use the Union clock; the 20-minute difference between the two armies' clocks (an unnamed estimate) is not applied. Heth's report puts Reynolds' death among the first shells of Pegram's guns, with no clock reading for it (a Confederate account of the cause).
weighing.independence: One group carries about 10.15: Wadsworth and Doubleday, whose hours and hedge are identical; independence is not shown, so the default is marked single-source. Weld, a separate witness, shows only that Reynolds was alive at about 10:00. The values 11:15 and 11:30 both come from Howard (and Schurz for the news hour).

source_panel_text: About 10:15 on Jul 1: Wadsworth's report of 4 Jul 1863 puts Reynolds' fall 'about 10.15 a. m.' and Doubleday's report repeats it. Howard's note of 5 p.m. says 11.15, but he was not at the fighting and was told about 11.30. The plan's 10:30 and 10:40-10:50 have no source. Six other values are listed.
